coverage_notes: Exhaustive survey across 6 database schema modeling/ERD tools in scope: Vertabelo (now Redgate Data Modeler), SqlDBM, QuickDBD, ERDPlus, pgModeler, and DBeaver. Coverage sweeps official homepages, documentation, pricing, G2/Capterra reviews (T2 review aggregators), company funding (Crunchbase/PitchBook—T2 databases), peer comparison articles (T1-T2 practitioner essays from dbschema.com, chartdb.io, talkingschema.ai, atlassian.com, holistics.io), and SourceForge/DBMS Tools comparison catalogs. Notably: Vertabelo was acquired by Redgate Software (Sept 2025, capital event captured at T1 official Redgate press release). G2 and Capterra provided quantified review counts and ratings (16-79 reviews per tool). Comparison articles from high-authority practitioners (dbschema.com, CTO Club, Atlassian, Holistics) provide HCI pain points (UI complexity, collaboration friction, diagram scalability limits). pgModeler as OSS community product tracked via GitHub releases and Sourceforge. DBeaver's freemium model and enterprise tier documented across official pages and Capterra. No Gartner Magic Quadrant specific to ERD tools found (Gartner coverage limited to broader BI/analytics); this gap noted. Deduplication: ~45 source URLs collected, consolidated to ~35 unique high-value entries by removing duplicates across aggregators, different regional Capterra/G2 pages, and article variations. Tiers assigned per market-research rubric: T0 = primary capture (official product pages, G2/Capterra aggregate review pages, Crunchbase/PitchBook profiles, press releases); T1 = official docs/changelogs/API docs, analyst coverage (Techzine, SD Times, Database Trends); T2 = high-quality practitioner essays (dbschema.com blog, CTO Club, Atlassian, Holistics, TalkingSchema, Devart, ChartDB blog, Medium author comparisons); T3 = community discussion (StackShare, SaaS Hub, alternativeTo, sourceforge comparison pages, listicles).
